title: Three ways to replicate stock: 95-delta call, synthetic, ZEBRA
summary: There are three ways to get stock-like exposure with options: a 95 delta call, a synthetic long (buy a call and sell a put at the same at-the-money strike), and a ZEBRA (two 70 delta calls against one short at-the-money call). All rise about the same on the upside but differ on the downside. The speaker prefers the 95 delta call: one option and no early assignment risk.

steps.caption: A $100 stock. We compare two ways to get the same exposure.
A 95 delta call: one option, almost all intrinsic value, limited loss.
A synthetic long: buy the $100 call, sell the $100 put. It moves like the stock both ways.
On the upside they match. On the downside the call's loss is capped; the synthetic keeps falling.
The ZEBRA (two 70 delta calls, one short ATM call) lands in between, and its Greeks change over time.
The speaker's choice: the 95 delta call. One leg, no early assignment risk.

takeaways: A 95 delta call, a synthetic and a ZEBRA all replicate stock on the upside.
They differ on the downside and in how their Greeks change over time.
The 95 delta call is the simplest: one option, no early assignment.
caveats: The backtest models the deep in-the-money call only, not the synthetic or ZEBRA.
Days to expiry are not given in the video; 120 days is illustrative.

scenario.label: 2018-2024: two bear markets and two rallies

backtest.note: Hold a 95-delta call as stock replacement, roll at 60 days left.
